articles.title: India is going offline again: New study reveals how consumers are moving away from digital payments in 2026
articles.summary: India’s lower-middle-class consumers are not abandoning digital channels, but 2026 data shows a surprising shift towards offline transactions. Bill payments, food orders and travel bookings have moved back to physical channels.

articles.title: ‘House rich, cash poor’: Why ₹2.20 lakh monthly salary doesn’t ensure wealth; LinkedIn post sparks discussion
articles.summary: A LinkedIn post highlighted financial challenges faced by professionals with high salaries but high expenses. Many save little due to lifestyle inflation.

articles.title: Grocery spending falls 8%, rent jumps 21%: How GST 2.0 is reshaping India's household budgets in 2026
articles.summary: Grocery spending fell 8% while rent rose 21%, showing a mixed picture for household budgets in 2026. GST 2.0 brought price relief, but families largely used the extra headroom for savings, better food, education, and health rather than splurging.

articles.title: Death of joint home loan borrower: Who pays the EMIs and who owns the house? SC advocate explains
articles.summary: A joint home loan does not automatically mean the surviving borrower gets full ownership of the house if the co-borrower dies. But the survivor remains liable for repaying the entire loan. Here’s what a Supreme Court advocate has to say about this.

articles.title: EPF nomination: Why updating your nominee after marriage and other life changes is important

articles.title: Gen Z spending habits: Convenience is key, prefer quick commerce and longer repayment tenure, finds report
articles.summary: Gen Z approaches credit and spending differently from older generations, according to a Kiwi report. Analysing user's spending habits it found they find convenience key, prefer quick commerce and longer repayment tenure.

articles.title: Filed ITR-4 last year? You might need to switch to ITR-3 in AY 2026-27 — here's why
articles.summary: Filing ITR-4 last year does not guarantee you can use the same form this year. Changes in income, business activity, investments, capital gains and other financial circumstances can affect eligibility. Taxpayers should check the key conditions before filing ITR-4 for AY 2026-27.

articles.title: SEBI eases NRI KYC rules: Will a fully digital route boost investments in India?

articles.title: NPS 100% equity option explained: How it works, who should consider it and key rules

articles.title: Want higher returns without taking much more risk? Add equity, then gold
